title: KCET 2013 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The process of zone refining is used in the purification of
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Zone refining relies on differing solubility of impurities in melt vs solid and is used to purify semiconductor-grade elements like germanium.

questions.q: The number of water molecules present in a drop of water weighing 0.018 gm is
Empirical formula of a compound is CH$_2$O and its molecular mass is 90, the molecular formula of the compound is
questions.explanation: Empirical formula mass of CH$_2$O = 30; n = 90/30 = 3, so molecular formula = (CH$_2$O)$_3$ = C$_3$H$_6$O$_3$.

questions.q: Hybridised states of carbon in Graphite and Diamond are respectively
questions.explanation: Graphite carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised (planar sheets) while diamond carbon is sp$^3$ hybridised (tetrahedral network).

questions.q: The mass of 112 cm$^3$ of NH$_3$ gas at STP is
IUPAC name of CH$_3$ - CH(OH) - CH$_2$ - CH(COOH) - CH$_3$ is
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Numbering the chain from the COOH carbon as C1, the methyl branch is at C2 and OH is at C4, giving 4-hydroxy-2-methylpentanoic acid.

questions.q: Alkali metals have negative reduction potential and hence they behave as
questions.explanation: A negative reduction potential means the metal readily loses electrons, i.e., it acts as a reducing agent.

questions.q: Which of the following gases has the highest value of RMS-velocity at 298 K ?
questions.explanation: RMS velocity is inversely proportional to $\sqrt{M}$; CH$_4$ (M=16) has the lowest molar mass among the options, so it has the highest RMS velocity.

questions.q: Cycloalkane formed when 1, 4-dibromopentane is heated with Sodium is
questions.explanation: Intramolecular Wurtz coupling joins C1 and C4 of pentane, forming a 4-membered ring with the C5 methyl group as a substituent, i.e., methylcyclobutane.

questions.q: In the reaction, 2FeSO$_4$ + H$_2$SO$_4$ + H$_2$O$_2$ $\rightarrow$ Fe$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$ + 2H$_2$O, the oxidizing agent is
questions.explanation: Fe$^{2+}$ is oxidised to Fe$^{3+}$ while H$_2$O$_2$ is reduced to H$_2$O, so H$_2$O$_2$ is the oxidizing agent.

questions.q: Given Thermochemical equation, 2H$_{2(g)}$ + O$_{2(g)}$ $\rightarrow$ 2H$_2$O$_{(l)}$; $\Delta$H = -571.6 kJ. Heat of decomposition of water is
questions.explanation: Formation of 2 mol water releases 571.6 kJ, so formation of 1 mol releases 285.8 kJ; decomposition of 1 mol water therefore requires +285.8 kJ.

questions.q: In Buna-S, the symbol 'Bu' stands for
questions.explanation: Buna-S is a copolymer of Butadiene and Styrene; 'Bu' stands for Butadiene.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of Cu$^{2+}$ ion is
questions.explanation: Cu atom is [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$; removing 2 electrons (4s first, then 3d) for Cu$^{2+}$ gives [Ar]3d$^9$4s$^0$.

questions.q: The yield of the products in the reaction, A$_{2(g)}$ + 2B$_{(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ C$_{(g)}$ + Q. kJ would be higher at
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic and decreases moles of gas (3 mol to 1 mol), so low temperature and high pressure favour higher yield by Le Chatelier's principle.

questions.q: Mesomeric effect involves
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: The mesomeric (resonance) effect is the delocalisation of $\pi$-electrons through conjugated systems.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets of ions represents the collection of isoelectronic species ?
questions.explanation: K$^+$, Ca$^{2+}$, Sc$^{3+}$ and Cl$^-$ all have 18 electrons, making them isoelectronic.

questions.q: Adsorption theory is applicable for
questions.explanation: The adsorption theory explains heterogeneous catalysis, where reactants are adsorbed on the catalyst surface.

questions.q: Methane can be converted into Ethane by the reactions
options: Chlorination followed by the reaction with alcoholic KOH.
Chlorination followed by the reaction with aqueous KOH.
questions.explanation: CH$_4$ is chlorinated to CH$_3$Cl, which undergoes the Wurtz reaction with Na to give ethane (C$_2$H$_6$).

questions.q: Intramolecular Hydrogen bonding is formed in
questions.explanation: In salicylaldehyde, the ortho -OH and -CHO groups form an intramolecular hydrogen bond within the same molecule.

questions.q: If 50% of the reactant is converted into a product in a first order reaction in 25 minutes, how much of it would react in 100 minutes ?
questions.explanation: Half-life = 25 min, so 100 min = 4 half-lives; fraction remaining = (1/2)$^4$ = 1/16, so 93.75% has reacted.

questions.q: The number of optical isomers of the compound CH$_3$ - CHBr - CHBr - COOH is
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: The molecule has two dissimilar chiral centres (C2 and C3 bear different sets of groups), giving 2$^2$ = 4 optical isomers.

questions.q: When limestone is heated, CO$_2$ is given off. The metallurgical operation is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Heating a carbonate ore to expel CO$_2$ is called calcination.

questions.q: The rate of reaction increases with rise in temperature because of
options: increase in number of activated molecules.
increase in the number of effective collisions.
questions.explanation: Raising temperature increases the number of molecules with energy above the activation energy, which also increases the number of effective collisions; the KEA key accepts both (1) and (4).

questions.q: Meso compounds do not show optical activity because
options: they do not contain chiral carbon atoms.
they have non-super imposable mirror images.
they do not contain plane of symmetry.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Meso compounds have chiral centres but also possess an internal plane of symmetry, making them achiral overall.

questions.q: When formic acid is heated with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$, the gas evolved is
questions.explanation: Conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ dehydrates formic acid (HCOOH) to release only CO gas.

questions.q: Temperature coefficient of a reaction is '2'. When temperature is increased from 30 °C to 90 °C, the rate of reaction is increased by
questions.explanation: A rise of 60 °C is six 10 °C intervals; rate increases by 2$^6$ = 64 times.

questions.q: Conversion of benzene to acetophenone can be brought by
questions.explanation: Benzene reacts with CH$_3$COCl/AlCl$_3$ in a Friedel-Crafts acylation to give acetophenone.

questions.q: Excess of PCl$_5$ reacts with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ giving
questions.explanation: With excess PCl$_5$, H$_2$SO$_4$ is converted further to sulphuryl chloride (SO$_2$Cl$_2$).

questions.q: An example for a neutral buffer is
questions.explanation: A mixture of a weak acid (acetic acid) and a weak base (ammonium hydroxide) of comparable strength gives a nearly neutral buffer.

questions.q: Least energetic conformation of cyclohexane is
questions.explanation: The intended correct answer is the chair conformation (lowest energy form of cyclohexane); the option is misprinted as 'Chain conformation', so KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates.

questions.q: Which of the following is employed in flash tubes in photography ?
questions.explanation: Both krypton and xenon are used to fill photographic flash tubes, so the KEA key accepts Kr and Xe.

questions.q: Conjugate base of H$_2$PO$_4^-$ is
questions.explanation: Removing one H$^+$ from H$_2$PO$_4^-$ gives its conjugate base HPO$_4^{2-}$.

questions.q: An alkyl bromide (X) reacts with Sodium in ether to form 4, 5-diethyl octane, the compound 'X' is
questions.explanation: Wurtz coupling of two molecules of 3-bromohexane (CH$_3$CH$_2$CH$_2$CHBrCH$_2$CH$_3$) joins at the C-Br carbons, giving an 8-carbon chain with ethyl branches at C4 and C5, i.e., 4,5-diethyloctane.

questions.q: Which one of the following shows highest magnetic moment ?
questions.explanation: Fe$^{2+}$ (d$^6$, high spin) has 4 unpaired electrons giving the highest magnetic moment ($\approx$4.90 BM) compared to Co$^{2+}$ and Cr$^{3+}$ (3 unpaired) and Ni$^{2+}$ (2 unpaired).

questions.q: The emf of a galvanic cell constituted with the electrodes Zn$^{2+}$ | Zn (- 0.76 V) and Fe$^{2+}$| Fe(-0.41 V) is
questions.explanation: Fe has the higher reduction potential so it is the cathode; EMF = E(cathode) - E(anode) = -0.41 - (-0.76) = +0.35 V.

questions.q:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched ?
I. RX + AgOH$_{(aq)}$ $ightarrow$ RH
II. RX + AgCN$_{(alco)}$ $ightarrow$ RNC
III. RX + KCN$_{(alco)}$ $ightarrow$ RNC
IV. RX + Na$_{(ether)}$ $ightarrow$ R-R
questions.explanation: AgCN (covalent, Ag-C bond) gives isocyanide (RNC) as major product, and RX with Na in ether undergoes the Wurtz reaction (R-R); so II and IV are correctly matched.

questions.q: In a transition series, with the increase in atomic-number, the paramagnetism
options: first increases to a maximum and then decreases
first decreases to a minimum and then increases
questions.explanation: The number of unpaired electrons rises to a maximum around the middle of the series (e.g., d$^5$) and then falls, so paramagnetism first increases then decreases.

questions.q: Identify a species which is 'NOT' a Bronsted acid but a Lewis acid.
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ has no proton to donate (not a Bronsted acid) but accepts an electron pair, making it a Lewis acid.

questions.q: The compound formed when calcium acetate and calcium formate is dry distilled.
questions.explanation: Dry distillation of a mixture of calcium acetate and calcium formate gives a mixed ketone-type reaction that yields acetaldehyde.

questions.q: d$^2$sp$^3$ hybridisation of the atomic orbitals gives
questions.explanation: d$^2$sp$^3$ (or sp$^3$d$^2$) hybridisation involves six orbitals directed octahedrally, giving an octahedral structure.

questions.q: The pH of 10$^{-8}$M HCl solution is
questions.explanation: At such low concentration, contribution of water's autoionization must be included: [H$^+$] $\approx$ 1.05$\times$10$^{-7}$ M, giving pH $\approx$ 6.9586, slightly less than 7.

questions.q: Which of the following is strongly acidic ?
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing -NO$_2$ group in p-nitrophenol stabilises the phenoxide ion, making it more acidic than phenol or cresols.

questions.q: A group of atoms can function as a ligand only when
options: it has an unshared electron pair.
it is a negatively charged ion.
it is a positively charged ion.
questions.explanation: A ligand donates a lone pair of electrons to the central metal atom/ion to form a coordinate bond.

questions.q: Which of the following is 'NOT' a colligative property ?
questions.explanation: All four listed properties are actually colligative properties, so the question has no valid 'NOT' answer; KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates.

questions.q: Acetone and Propanal are
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Acetone (a ketone) and propanal (an aldehyde) have the same molecular formula C$_3$H$_6$O but different functional groups, so they are functional isomers.

questions.q: Which of the following is diamagnetic ?
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, N$_2$ has all electrons paired (bond order 3, no unpaired electrons), making it diamagnetic, unlike H$_2^+$, He$_2^+$ and O$_2$.

questions.q: 3 gms of urea is dissolved in 45 gms of H$_2$O. The relative lowering in vapour pressure is
questions.explanation: Moles urea = 3/60 = 0.05; moles water = 45/18 = 2.5; relative lowering $\approx$ n(solute)/n(solvent) = 0.05/2.5 = 0.02.

questions.q: The reagent used to distinguish between acetaldehyde and benzaldehyde is
questions.explanation: Fehling's solution gives a positive test (red precipitate) only with aliphatic aldehydes like acetaldehyde, not with benzaldehyde, so it distinguishes the two.

questions.q: Metallic lustre is due to
options: high polish on the surface of metals
reflection of light by mobile electrons
questions.explanation: Delocalised mobile electrons in the metallic lattice reflect incident light, giving metals their characteristic lustre.

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solutions will exhibit highest boiling point ?
questions.explanation: Effective particle concentration (i $\times$ C) is highest for 0.01 M Na$_2$SO$_4$ (i=3, giving 0.03), producing the greatest boiling point elevation.

questions.q: Which one of the following gives amine on heating with amide ?
questions.explanation: This is the Hofmann bromamide degradation, normally carried out with Br$_2$ in aqueous KOH; the KEA key also accepts Br$_2$ in alcoholic KOH.

questions.q: The number of antibonding electrons present in O$_2^-$ molecular ion is
questions.explanation: In the valence MO configuration of the superoxide ion O$_2^-$ (17 valence electrons), the antibonding electrons are $\sigma^*2s^2$ and $\pi^*2p^3$, i.e., 5; ambiguity over whether to count 1s core antibonding electrons led KEA to award a grace mark.

questions.q: The process is spontaneous at the given temperature, if
options: $\Delta$H is +ve and $\Delta$S is equal to zero
questions.explanation: $\Delta$G = $\Delta$H - T$\Delta$S is always negative when $\Delta$H is negative and $\Delta$S is positive, so the process is spontaneous at all temperatures.

questions.q: Glucose when reduced with HI and Red Phosphorus gives
questions.explanation: Strong reduction (HI/red P) of the 6-carbon chain of glucose removes all oxygen functionalities, giving n-hexane.

questions.q: The stability of a Lyophobic colloid is due to
options: Adsorption of covalent molecules on the colloid
questions.explanation: Lyophobic colloidal particles carry a like charge, and the resulting electrostatic repulsion prevents them from aggregating, providing stability.

questions.q: Oils are liquids at room temperature since they contain higher percentage of
questions.explanation: Oleates (esters of unsaturated oleic acid) have lower melting points due to kinks from the C=C double bond, keeping oils liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: Which of the following cations will have minimum flocculation value for arsenic sulphide sol ?
questions.explanation: Arsenic sulphide sol is negatively charged; by the Hardy-Schulze rule, the cation with the highest charge (Al$^{3+}$) has the minimum flocculation value.

questions.q: The value of entropy of solar system is
questions.explanation: By the second law of thermodynamics, the entropy of an isolated system such as the (approximately isolated) solar system/universe keeps increasing.

questions.q: In face centred cubic lattice, a unit cell is shared equally by how many unit cells ?
questions.explanation: In any cubic lattice (including FCC), a corner atom of a unit cell is shared equally among 8 adjacent unit cells.

questions.q: The number of disulphide linkages present in Insulin are
questions.explanation: The insulin protein contains 3 disulphide (-S-S-) linkages holding its two peptide chains together.
